facts.text: Barnacle Bill Rock was deployed at Ares Vallis during Mars Pathfinder in 1997.

The first rock analysed by Sojourner's APXS instrument was informally named 'Barnacle Bill'. Analysis revealed it was rich in silicon, similar to andesite found on Earth. This was surprising — scientists expected basaltic compositions. It suggested Mars had a more complex geological history than previously thought.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Revealed a silicon-rich andesitic composition that overturned the assumption Mars had only simple basaltic geology, proving a more complex volcanic history.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Ares Vallis.
Barnacle Bill still sits where Sojourner analysed it, an ordinary-looking rock that changed our understanding of Martian geology.
